title: A Hare Across the Shoulders

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: A hare comes down off the ridge across a man's shoulders and the yard asks what the carrying cost; the man tells it the weather. The kiln takes its coal before the basket is fed and gives four pulls where a man would look for five. Bone is a month of directions and not figures.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of the Clay Yard, told to the well and the kiln-mouth in Bone

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a body of three hundred to three hundred and two days, six months and one hundred and twenty to one hundred and twenty-two days, carried everywhere in a basket and told by nobody. The surgeon's register colours the noticing and is never a break in the narration: the body inventoried as a wound of crust, unnamed gap, frozen thread, cold at cheek, temple and wrist and an afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform; the three hundredth morning kept as a round threshold and not paid; the carried fire kept in fours with the fifth unpaid and its payer unnamed; the three counts in three places that do not become one; six hearings of the full note beside and never among with the seventh place kept empty; the told bell kept beside the heard in its square; the told figure beside the paid with Frost's three arithmetics locked in Berr Clay's box up the clay road, one in twelve printed and unchallenged and no signature on the space between; the dressed grain turned beneath the wool with a progressively lighter touch and given no figure; the stayed frost, skinned trough and silt-clouded plate of ice called weather and entered nowhere; nine hands with Ilva's ninth strip unread and no tenth, the row at five askings with one shaping and no witness, the Frost 14 well-saying held at three shapings beside Hessa Rale's eighth hand with a finger between every pair, nine stoppings with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end, Tarn's loan uncalled, Jorra's promise ungiven and he's not Vail sealed, Garl held in objects with his name unspoken, the house's not-doings kept on a place apart from the boy's own gaps with a finger between; and the six small coordinations of the hand entered on the sixth place and never promoted into a reach, a hearing, a seventh, a stopping, a payment, a held change, a key, a power, a freedom, a gift, a doctrine or a rule. On Bone 2 the household's first firing of the month is the chapter's one meaningful change, advanced and not paid: the hand goes to the widow's mark before the kiln, one breath, let go, the carried coal under the back of a broken pot, the fire answering in fours with the fifth missing and nobody praiseing it, naming what it mended, entering a slate or making a lesson of it. A hunter come down from Cold Acre is glimpsed at the well with a hare across his shoulders, the month's trade entering as a direction and not a figure, a walk-on given no name and no sheet.
places: the flat stone by the well

scenes.title: The Three Hundredth Morning
scenes.synopsis: First of six entries, the chapter's only \dropcap and its first \daymark{300}{Bone 1, Firstday, Y.H. 813}: the small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof into the first light of an ordinary Firstday with no market, Cross or bell. Open on the hand laid down against the fold on the one hundred and seventy-fourth answer as a tool put away where the next hand will find it without looking; do not recap Chapter 82, the reader has just read it. Bone comes on without a boundary drawn and neither of the district's two habits of naming its months is set right or left wrong. Carry 299 to 300 exact, six months and one hundred and twenty days told by nobody --- a round threshold kept, not paid, not a milestone spoken over the basket (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth unpaid three hundred days with its payer unnamed (T088); Garl's name unspoken three hundred days. Body inventory in the surgeon's old order: one stiff leathery brown-edged barley crust two inches from the ear, gone past the point where a child would eat it, its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread of drool frozen in the dry heat and unwiped, because nobody under any roof has ever been given an instruction about the thread and a basket set down is a pot set down and left; cold stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint as at the end of a line written out for it; the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody in this house will perform. He knows the composed face that is not composure, that a cold patient cannot clot and will seem better before he is worse, and that a man must be warmed from the outside and slowly; he wants the crust lifted two inches and cannot close two inches on the pot handle, both true and the second louder, entered nowhere (T060/T086). Three counts in three places --- the kiln's four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should stand under the floor, the river's water over water at the finger's-width door, the boards' four nails, four and a thumb-width knot --- and agreeing any two would want a payer put under both and none stands. Six hearings beside and never among with the seventh place kept empty, the heard bell beside the told in its square, the told figure beside the paid with all three Frost arithmetics gone up the road and the figure read still not the figure paid, three readings three and not one account with the finding on a place of its own and no payer (T061/T082, T078, T015/T041/T047). Sella goes to the fire before the basket, tells the coals it is the thaw, turns them with the back of a broken pot and says 'The house will keep it', keeps her finger above the charcoal, her lips along the two-gapped row, sets the pot rim two inches out with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, and does not touch the widow's mark, because a morning is not an opening (T058/T079, T100). Outside the wool the hand goes up an inch and takes a small intake from the room whose floor does not touch his, holds it against the kiln's fourth low pull and lets it go whole on the same note without carrying it into the missing fifth: the **one hundred and seventy-fifth** answer, exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air, promoted into no reach, hearing, seventh, payment, gift, doctrine or rule. The surgeon's clean satisfaction at the exact coordination is checked by the infant's louder want of the crust, and the checking is the work and he does not call it a virtue.

scenes.title: The Month's Trade
scenes.synopsis: Second entry of Day 300, no new dated heading: afternoon of Bone 1 through the going of the light and into the small hours at the Clay Yard, the yard well and its flat stone, the drying racks and rack end, the kindling and flagstones, the wheel-shed edge, the back room as a direction and a sound, the bed, the boards and the towel. Sella carries him down at the half-pace from every open slate and goes wide around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number: the clean dark line at the Vail corner and the finer grey hairline beside it called the thaw, unswept both; the space beneath the lowest rack with its broken birth-slates; the round ring where the shallow pan once stood with no scrape, crumb, print, chip or word; the trough skinned over; the field's empty place out on the worked strips; the returning-line place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried, T060/T086). The stayed frost on the north lip, the skinned water and the silt-clouded plate of ice set on the flat stone out of the path of feet are three coverings in three places, all called weather, kept with a finger between and no fourth likeness made a cause and no payer named (T083/T085 held). The dressed grain is turned beneath the wool with a progressively lighter touch and no figure; three Frost readings went over it without knowing what it cost and the space between figure and price stays unsigned (T077). **New texture of the month, a walk-on given no name and no sheet:** a hunter come down from Cold Acre waits his turn at the well with a hare across his shoulders, its weight judged by the carrying arm and not by a figure. A woman asks what the carrying cost and the man tells her the weather and goes off toward the north gate road; nobody turns twice, no slate is opened, no price is spoken and the month's trade enters as a direction and not an account (T077 advanced, not paid). The boy does not join the hare to the missing hand, the dressed grain, the cold foot or the fire's fifth; a cost asked as a direction and answered with the weather leaves no entry. At the kindling Tarn keeps six in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh at the lip beside Garl's unforged collector sentence, tells the wood 'Six counted. The next I don't count', brings the ear-sentence to the calling word as a remembered ninth stopping with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end, draws the breath he does not spend and keeps the Seed 16 breath unspent; his stroke goes over the shallow bright patch without the half-check, Ash stays worked into the knuckle creases, the pale clip-ring holds what light there is, the warm loft stone is cold and unreconciled by not trying, the loan stays uncalled and no collector comes up or down the clay road (T036/T076, T006, T009/T013/T092). Jorra comes through with meal-fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent finger, parts dusty and clean forearms as clot from vessel, speaks to the wheel and a pot before any person, knows the full note three turns ahead and withholds it on the near-full tray beside the hearings and never among them, and puts his bent finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence; men unnamed go low into the back room before first grey and get no name; the burned slate stands at four, the shut-room tellings at two, the pot sayings at three with the Smoke 14 note apart, the row at five askings with one shaping and no witness; 'he's not Vail' stays sealed and the promise of the foundling's name neither given nor withdrawn (T035/T031/T062, T065/T095, T101, T064 held). Outside the wool the hand takes two small intakes from the next room and holds them apart with a finger between, letting the nearer one end early and keeping that early ending whole as an absence: the **one hundred and seventy-sixth** answer, exact and worth nothing, not a joining, a hearing, a payment or a rule. Last image: the flat stone by the well with the clouded plate of ice standing out of the path of feet, and the hand coming down on the river's low note with the gap left a gap.

scenes.title: The Mark Before the Kiln
scenes.synopsis: Third entry, third dated \daymark{301}{Bone 2, Secondday, Y.H. 813}: the small hours under the Vail roof into the first light of an ordinary Secondday, at the hearth and the kiln mouth. New day, new date, no recap; nothing seen at the well yesterday is brought into this morning as a lesson, sign, mending, witness or payment. Carry 300 to 301 exact, six months and one hundred and twenty-one days told by nobody (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth unpaid three hundred and one days, payer unnamed (T088). **THE CHAPTER'S ONE MEANINGFUL CHANGE, ADVANCED AND NOT PAID (T058/T079, T088):** the household fires in Bone and the first opening stands on Bone 2, earned by that morning's own light. Sella goes to the kiln mouth before she comes to the basket, puts her hand to the widow's mark on its cord at her throat, holds it one breath, lets go, lifts the clay lid with the back of a hand and tips the carried coal under the back of a broken pot; the fire takes and answers four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should have stood, its payer unnamed three hundred and one days. Nobody praises the opening, names what it mended, enters a slate or makes a lesson of it; five openings in five months are five and not a rule, and the four behind the household (150, 180, 240, 271) are not looked at again as signs, lessons, payments or menders (T058/T079). The boy takes the small intake from the next room at the very moment of the opening and holds it against the first low pull without carrying it into the fire's missing fifth; the hand goes down on the river's note as it always does and the gap stays a gap: the **one hundred and seventy-seventh** answer, exact, complete and worth nothing, not a reach, a hearing, a seventh, a stopping, a payment, a held change, a gift, a doctrine or a rule. He keeps the fifth opening on a place of its own with a finger between it and his own kept gaps, and does not lay it across the house's not-doings or the covered grain; a joining would want a payer and none stands to either. The widow's mark is not touched again at a shelf, a well, a rack, a basket, a yard, an afternoon or a going of the light on any of these three days, because the hand goes to the mark before the kiln and at no other hour. The surgeon reads the opening as a controlled reconnection under a clamp, knows that heat returned from outside is paid for by somebody and that nobody in the room will name the payer, and the reading buys him nothing at two inches of air. Last image: the lifted clay lid held in the back of a hand over the broken pot while the fire takes in fours and the fifth stays a silence under the floor.

scenes.title: Five Are Five
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry, no new dated heading: afternoon of Bone 2 through the going of the light and into the small hours at the Clay Yard, the well and flat stone, the rack end, the kindling and flagstones, the wheel-shed edge, the loaf shelf, bed, boards and towel. Afternoon thins without ending the way heat goes out of a pot lifted off the coals and set on a cold stone; heat draws back from cheek, temple and wrist and the inventory is renewed in the old order, exact and unentered (T061/T082, T060/T086). The morning's opening is not looked at again: no slate was entered, no lesson made, no name given to what it mended, and the carried fire still misses its fifth under the floor, unpaid three hundred and one days with its payer unnamed, so a real opening settles no account (T058/T079, T088). Sella turns the dressed grain beneath the wool with a progressively lighter touch and gives it no figure, goes wide around the seven walked-around places, and calls the stayed frost, the skinned trough and the clouded plate of ice weather entered nowhere with no fourth likeness made a cause (T077, T083/T085 held, T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). At the well Ilva of the firing work is seen once drawing with the pail against her knee, clay dried pale in the crescents of her nails and grey rack dust in the seam of one thumb she does not scrub out; asked what the month's firings have taken, her hand goes toward her sleeve and stays there, the short notched birch strip not taken out, read, copied, counted or joined to any slate, and no figure comes off the wood; her eyes go to the asker and her mouth opens after both: 'Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account.' The boy takes the order of reaching and files no tenth record-first hand; the ninth stays nine with a finger between it and the eighth, and nothing of the well goes under the roof as lesson, figure, mending, cause or payment (T080 held and advanced, not paid). At the kindling Tarn keeps six where the house can check and the seventh at the lip, tells the wood 'Six counted. The next I don't count', remembers the ninth stopping with no tenth and keeps the Seed 16 breath unspent, the loan uncalled and no collector on the road (T036/T076). Jorra comes through with the day's meal-fine grey dust, speaks to the wheel and a pot before any person, withholds the note he knows three turns ahead and sets his bent finger into the cold damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence; he gives the men in the back room no name and does not say the room is cold (T035/T031/T062). Outside the wool the hand holds the fourth low pull from under the floor and a small letting-go from the next room on two places with a finger between, neither carried into the other: the **one hundred and seventy-eighth** answer, exact, complete and worth nothing, not a joining, a seventh or a payment. Last image: the pot rim set two inches beyond the reaching hand with its handle turned toward it and a half-beat before Sella went away without a look toward the bed.

scenes.title: The Number Passing Over
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry, fifth dated \daymark{302}{Bone 3, Thirdday, Y.H. 813}: the small hours under the Vail roof into the first light of an ordinary Thirdday, at the bed, the loaf shelf, the boards, the hearth and the towel. New day, new date, no recap; the opening two mornings ago is not brought in as a sign, a mended account or the fifth of a rule. Carry 301 to 302 exact, six months and one hundred and twenty-two days told by nobody (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth unpaid three hundred and two days with its payer unnamed, Garl's name unspoken three hundred and two days (T088, T009/T013/T092). The round three hundred went over on Bone 1 and was kept as a threshold and not spent; nothing marked its passing under this roof and the count has gone on into 301 and 302 with nobody telling him what any of them counts. Body inventory in the old order: one stiff brown-edged crust two inches off with its unnamed empty place and no third, the thread frozen in the dry heat and unwiped, cold stopping at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint as at the end of a line written out for it, the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody will perform; he knows the ease cold puts on a face is not ease and that a man must be warmed from the outside and slowly; he wants the crust lifted and cannot close two inches on the pot handle, both true and the second louder (T060/T086). Three counts in three places that do not become one; six hearings beside and never among with the seventh empty; the heard bell in its square beside the told; the told figure beside the paid with Frost's three arithmetics locked up the road and no signature on the space between; three readings three and not one account with the finding on a place of its own and no payer; nine stoppings with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end; the row at five askings with one shaping and no witness; the Frost 14 saying at three shapings beside Hessa Rale's eighth hand; nine hands with Ilva's ninth unread; the burned slate at four and the shut-room tellings at two; the seventh green a colour and the seventh shape a shape with no eighth (T061/T082, T078, T015/T041/T047, T036/T076, T101, T080, T065/T095, T050/T051 and T033/T034 held). Sella goes to the fire before the basket, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot and says 'The house will keep it', keeps her finger above the charcoal and her lips along the two-gapped row, and leaves the widow's mark untouched, for a morning is not an opening (T058/T079, T100). Outside the wool the hand sets an empty interval beside a held interval, brings the finger down between them and takes it up, leaving both where they were: the **one hundred and seventy-ninth** answer, a keeping and not a spending, exact, complete and worth nothing, not a reach, a hearing, a joining, a payment, a gift, a doctrine or a rule. Last image: the finger between the two intervals coming away and leaving them parted by the width of a finger on the towel at the head of the bed.

scenes.title: The Hand Laid Down
scenes.synopsis: Sixth and final entry, chapter close, no new dated heading: Day 302, Bone 3, the going of the light and the small hours at the Clay Yard, the yard well and flat stone, the hearth, loaf shelf, bed, boards and towel. Bone goes on without a boundary drawn and neither of the district's two habits of naming its months is set right or left wrong; the month's hunts and repairs stay directions judged by the carrying arm and the weather, never figures, and the yard goes around its seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried, T077). Frost's three arithmetics with their true subtractions ride locked up the clay road in Berr Clay's box with one in twelve printed and unchallenged and the figure read still not the figure paid; three readings are three and not one account and the finding stays on a place of its own with no payer, not a lesson, grievance, mending or doctrine and not laid across the house's not-doings, the covered grain or the boy's own kept gaps, the edges nearly touching and the finger going between (T015/T041/T047, T061/T082). Afternoon thins without ending; heat draws back from the fold; the inventory is renewed in the old order and the surgeon's knowing that a cold patient cannot clot and will seem better before he is worse buys nothing at two inches of air (T060/T086). Sella went to the fire before the basket, told it the thaw, turned the coals with the back of a broken pot and said 'The house will keep it', kept her finger above the charcoal, moved her lips along a row standing with two gaps and gave neither gap a figure, glanced once at the clay jar standing cold under its lead glaze, set the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, and did not touch the widow's mark, because a going of the light is not an opening and five openings in five months are five and not a rule (T058/T079, T100). At the kindling Tarn keeps six in the thumb-mark and the seventh at the lip beside Garl's unforged collector sentence with the ear-sentence stopped at the calling word as a remembered ninth stopping and no tenth before the seventh year at its very end, the Seed 16 breath unspent, the warm loft stone cold and unreconciled by not trying, the loan uncalled and no collector on the road (T036/T076, T006). Jorra keeps his grey dust and his silence, his bent finger going into the cold damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence, the burned slate at four, the shut-room tellings at two, 'he's not Vail' sealed and the promise ungiven (T035/T031/T062, T065/T095). Garl stays in objects: the salt-stiff coat with its left-shoulder crease, the hollow wheel-seat, the clean dark line and its finer grey, the proverb said to the pot and the fire, the uncalled tile debt worse for being uncalled, his name unspoken three hundred and two days (T009/T013/T092). The small keepings stay small: Ilva's strip in a sleeve, the three shapings of the well-saying on a place of their own beside the eighth hand, the row at five askings with no witness, the seventh green a colour and the seventh shape a shape with no eighth, the charcoal under the shelf, the reed-cutter's cord and the soft-cuffed clerk's inward slate each where it lies, none brought forward as a sign, lesson, mending, cause or payment, and nothing joined, named, opened, called, paid or ended (T080, T101, T050/T051, T033/T034, T100, T099, T090). Outside the wool the hand comes up an inch toward the river's note; at the very end of the day a small intake stands whole and he lets it go on the same note without carrying it into the fire's missing fifth, the bell's gap left in the square or the river's low over lower: the **one hundred and eightieth** answer, exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air, promoted into no reach, hearing, seventh, stopping, payment, held change, key, power, freedom, gift, doctrine or rule, and no payer named to it. The surgeon's clean satisfaction at the exact coordination is checked by the infant's louder want of the crust two inches off, and the checking is the work and he does not call it a virtue. The hand comes down on the river's note and the gap stays a gap, and he does not fill the gap to make the row come out even. Three hundred and two stands exact, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody in Low Kiln, Sill and Grath; six months and one hundred and twenty-two days are told by nobody; the fire's fifth is unpaid the same number of days with its payer unnamed; Garl's name has not been spoken under the roof the same number of days; one hundred and eighty honest answers stand on the sixth place, each an object and not a power, and neither the number nor the small hand-movings that made them stand up and call themselves a doctrine, for a doctrine is an account that has found a payer and none stood. Bone 4 (Day 303) and Bone 10 (Day 309), the month's first Account-day, stand ahead and are not brought into a day that has not earned them. The hand laid itself back against the fold as a man puts away a tool where the next hand will find it without looking. The file lies open on the towel at the head of the bed with every gap left gap, every tray parted by a finger's width and nothing that had moved. The river's low note goes quiet under the finger's-width door, and out on the flat stone by the well the plate of ice stands clouded with silt out of the path of feet, and Bone goes on without a boundary drawn.
